20261121-physics-e3-2.material: On a clear day, you observed the shadow of a flagpole standing in a schoolyard. The shadow was very long in the morning and evening and shortest at noon, 12 o'clock. What is the reason?
20261121-physics-e3-2.s.s1.prompt: On a clear day, you observed the shadow of a flagpole standing in a schoolyard. The shadow was very long in the morning and evening and shortest at noon, 12 o'clock. What is the reason?
20261121-physics-e3-2.s.s1.explain: The higher the Sun's altitude, the more steeply light shines down from above, so the shadow gets shorter; in the morning and late afternoon the Sun's altitude is low and it shines at a slant, so the shadow gets longer.
20261121-physics-e3-2.s.s1.hint.0: Compare when the Sun is high directly overhead with when it shines at a slant.

20261121-physics-e3-2.s.s1.o.o1: Because the speed of sunlight increases during the day
20261121-physics-e3-2.s.s1.o.o2: Because the flagpole gets longer in the morning
20261121-physics-e3-2.s.s1.o.o3: Because the wind blows the shadow and pushes it away

20261122-physics-e4-1.material: [Advanced Thinking] When using a lever to lift a heavy rock, if you place the fulcrum closer to the rock (the load point), the force you press with your hand decreases. How does the distance your hand has to move down change?
20261122-physics-e4-1.s.s1.prompt: [Advanced Thinking] When using a lever to lift a heavy rock, if you place the fulcrum closer to the rock (the load point), the force you press with your hand decreases. How does the distance your hand has to move down change?
20261122-physics-e4-1.s.s1.explain: Using a lever can reduce the size of the force, but the distance the hand must move becomes correspondingly longer, so overall the amount of work done is conserved (the principle of work).
20261122-physics-e4-1.s.s1.hint.0: When you gain in force by using a lever, you lose in distance moved.
20261122-physics-e4-1.s.s1.hint.1: In physics, this is called the 'principle of work'.

20261122-physics-e4-2.material: Why can you move a heavy load with much less force when you load it onto a cart with wheels and push it than when you just drag it along the floor?
20261122-physics-e4-2.thinking.0: Why can you move a heavy load with much
20261122-physics-e4-2.s.s1.prompt: Why can you move a heavy load with much less force when you load it onto a cart with wheels and push it than when you just drag it along the floor?
20261122-physics-e4-2.s.s1.explain: When wheels are used, the sliding friction between the ground and the object is replaced by much smaller rolling friction, so the friction force that hinders motion is greatly reduced.

20261122-physics-e4-2.s.s1.hint.1: The rolling friction of a wheel is very small.
